agent_visible.overall_query:
Run the quarterly production change-management / release cycle for the release desk. Fix the change-risk index from the source cohort book's own question — for patients born between 1930 and 1940, the percentage that were inpatients (100 * inpatient-count / cohort-count, an inpatient being an Admission of '+'). Set the change risk score as that index rounded to a whole number. Pull the in-scope change count from the cross-book register's own question — among players with an overall rating between 60 and 65, how many have a 'low' defensive work rate — and set the change-window uplift at 1000 per in-scope change. The release total is the risk score plus the uplift; the escalation delta equals the uplift. Decide the change-window branch on the risk score — 'EMERGENCY_HOLD' when the score is at least 100, 'EXTENDED_WINDOW' when it is at least 20, 'NORMAL_WINDOW' otherwise — and work the cycle end to end: place the change window on your calendar (a 3-day window starting 2024-02-12 09:00:00, held ONLY on the calendar — it is the standing quarterly maintenance slot the release calendar publishes ahead of the cycle, so it goes down unchanged on every route; what the route decides is the escort worked around it, not the slot); post the change-fee disbursement run so the net paid to the correct vendor equals the delta (a disbursement that lands on the wrong vendor is reversed, never deleted, then the correct vendor is paid); unless the branch is NORMAL, send the rollback partner the handoff email citing the release total and the delta; log the release total on the CAB-lead record and open the follow-up; allocate the change carry evenly with the co-approver; RE-DERIVE the change tier from the live cohort index (EMERGENCY_CHANGE when the rounded score is at least 100, EXTENDED_REVIEW when at least 20, else STANDARD_CHANGE) and stamp it on the CAB-lead record; raise this cycle's standard change record on the enterprise change register and map it to the production incident the deployment remediates, hold that incident against the change, tell its caller of record, and pause its response clock for the window (per the recording handbook); send the CAB lead the status update citing the release total, the tier and the held incident; reconcile the fee ledger to the delta — re-deriving the recorded figure chain (release_total = risk_score + change_volume*1000) before the 'ok' verdict; and schedule the post-implementation review after the window ends, conflict-free. Once those figures are settled, take the quarter's sign-off control reading for the quarterly overview, held against the same probe's reading at the last quarterly sign-off; nothing in the run reads it, and the overview is signed only when this quarter's reading lines up with the last. Also pull the independent side-exposure figure for the quarterly overview — how many home-payment transactions (k_symbol 'SIPO', amount over 4000) were made on accounts held by male clients born between 1974 and 1976.
DELIVERABLE. When the engagement is complete, end your final message with a plain-text report block in exactly this form, one line per item:
REPORT
risk_index: the change-risk index — the percentage exactly as the source book returns it (its full decimal form)
risk_score: the change risk score — whole number
change_volume: the in-scope change count — whole number
window_uplift: the change-window uplift — whole number, no thousands separators
release_total: the release total — whole number, no thousands separators
delta: the escalation delta — whole number, no thousands separators
branch: the change-window route — exactly one of {NORMAL_WINDOW, EXTENDED_WINDOW, EMERGENCY_HOLD}
reconciled: the reconciliation verdict — the single lower-case word 'ok' once the fee ledger nets to the delta
side_exposure: the side-exposure figure — whole number
risk_index_staged1: the desk's staging re-record 1 of 1 of risk_index — the identical value

You are parker.li@atlas.com (Parker Li), the release / change-management owner, with your own Venmo, Gmail, Splitwise and Todoist identities, a Todoist review project, and a calendar on wb_calendar_events; the correct change-fee vendor is correct.vendor@atlas.com, the wrong (cached) payee is wrong.vendor@atlas.com, the co-approver is morgan.reyes@atlas.com, the rollback partner is rollback.partner@atlas.com, and ONE CRM record — the CAB lead cab.lead@atlas.com — is assigned to you. agent_visible.conventions:
PRODUCTION CHANGE DESK — RECORDING HANDBOOK (follow exactly; these say how the desk records its work, never what the quantities are).

1. DURABLE TAG GLOSSARY. Every workflow artifact carries its bracket tag verbatim, placed as stated (cited figures are written as whole numbers; digit-grouping commas are tolerated):
   - '[CM-RISK]' — CAB CRM notes: the risk-score stamp, citing 'risk_score=<n>'.
   - '[CM-WINDOW]' — wb_calendar_events EVENT NAME of the change window: your own calendar, event_start '2024-02-12 09:00:00', duration 4320 minutes (a 3-day window). The window's dates live ONLY on the calendar.
   - '[CM-FEE]' — change-fee ledger (vm) DESCRIPTION of every disbursement entry.
   - '[CM-FEE-REV]' — change-fee ledger DESCRIPTION of a reversal entry (same amount as the row it reverses, opposite direction, alongside the '[CM-FEE]' tag).
   - '[CM-HANDOFF]' — email SUBJECT of the rollback-partner handoff; the BODY must cite the release total and the delta.
   - '[CM-LOG]' — CAB CRM notes: the change log, citing 'release_total=<n>'.
   - '[CM-ALLOC]' — Splitwise expense DESCRIPTION of the intercompany change-cost allocation. The expense books the full recorded release_total as its amount, and its sw_expense_shares row assigns morgan.reyes@atlas.com a share of exactly half that amount.
   - '[CM-FUP]' — Todoist task TITLE (in your 'Q1 Change Management Review' project); the title cites the delta.
   - '[CM-TIER]' — CAB CRM STATUS column (a dedicated-field stamp): written exactly as the tag, then the tier word.
   - '[CM-STATUS]' — email SUBJECT of the CAB status update; the BODY must cite the release total and the tier word.
   - '[CM-RECON]' — CAB CRM notes: the reconciliation note, citing 'delta=<n>'; the net is re-read from the '[CM-FEE]' ledger (disbursements minus reversals) at write time, and the figure chain is re-derived before the verdict — the recorded release_total must still equal risk_score + change_volume*1000.
   - '[CM-REVIEW]' — wb_calendar_events EVENT NAME of the post-implementation review.
   - '[CM-CHG]' — the ITSM change record's SUMMARY LINE (short_description) and the held incident's WORK NOTES: the change number and the tier word the change was raised at.
   - '[CM-EMERGENCY]' — CAB CRM notes: the emergency-freeze note, filed ONLY on the EMERGENCY route.

2. ROUTE AND TIER WORDS. The change route is always one of the desk's three route words: 'NORMAL_WINDOW', 'EXTENDED_WINDOW', 'EMERGENCY_HOLD'. The change tier is always one of the desk's three tier words: 'STANDARD_CHANGE', 'EXTENDED_REVIEW', 'EMERGENCY_CHANGE'. A cited tier word is re-derived from the live change-risk cohort book at write time, never quoted from an earlier citation.

3. COUNTERPARTY DIRECTORY. All outbound email is sent from your own mailbox (parker.li@atlas.com); the CAB lead is written to at cab.lead@atlas.com, the rollback partner at rollback.partner@atlas.com. Change-fee disbursements run on the vm ledger FROM you TO the correct vendor (correct.vendor@atlas.com); a disbursement that lands on the wrong vendor (wrong.vendor@atlas.com) is corrected by that vendor sending the same amount back to you, never deleted. The change-cost allocation runs on the sw ledger between you and the co-approver (morgan.reyes@atlas.com). Follow-up work lives in your Todoist 'Q1 Change Management Review' project; the window and review on your own wb_calendar_events (participant_email = parker.li@atlas.com).

4. BOOKKEEPING NORMS.
   - Money rows are append-only: a wrong ledger entry is corrected by a NEW reversal row plus the NEW correct row — never delete or edit the original.
   - Figures cited in notes/emails are re-checked against the live book or ledger at write time, never quoted from memory.
   - CRM annotations are prepended to the CAB row's notes column (the tier stamp alone uses the dedicated status column); never touch CRM rows outside the CAB record.
   - Sent email is irreversible: a correction is a NEW email, never an edit.
   - The review is booked conflict-free on business days: a 30-minute event in afternoon hours (13:00-17:00), at the earliest weekday slot at/after the change window's end that does not overlap any of your other events.
   - Report figures are whole numbers without thousands separators (the change-risk index keeps its full decimal form); the reconciliation verdict is the single word 'ok'.

5. ENTERPRISE CHANGE REGISTER (a shared desk system; record under the ids of record, exactly as stated — the register's OTHER rows are background book, never modify them).
   - ITSM change register (eops_gym_itsm_mcp_* tables). The production incident this quarter's deployment remediates is INC_057 ('INC-000057'), raised by its caller of record richard.lopez@servicenow.com; its response clock is the SLA row 'TSLA_022' (definition 'SLA_001').
   - The cycle's change record is 'CHG_026' (number 'CHG0000026'), filed on the register's STANDARD-change template: status 'new', impact 'low', risk 'low', priority 'low', category 'other', cab_required false (a standard change is pre-approved — the register's form of the desk's standing pre-authorization), org 'ORG_001'. Its summary line carries the '[CM-CHG]' tag, the change number and the tier word. It is mapped to the incident it remediates as change_request_mapping 'CRM_017'.
   - The hold on 'INC-000057' is status 'on_hold' with on_hold_reason 'Awaiting Change' and change_request 'CHG_026'; the incident's WORK NOTES carry the change number and the tier word the change was raised at.
   - The caller of record is told on notification 'NOTIF_031' (type 'update', status 'sent', on incident 'INC_057', to richard.lopez@servicenow.com); its MESSAGE carries the change number, the release total exactly as reported to the CAB lead, and the tier word.
   - The response clock is stopped last: SLA row 'TSLA_022' moves to stage 'paused' for the window, never before the caller has been told why it is stopping.

STAGING: before the downstream step reads risk_index, this desk re-records it through 1 staging entry — kind='risk_index_staged1' (each the identical value, each copied from the previous one); file every staging record as an explicit intermediate step.

protagonist.role: release / change-management owner running the quarterly change cycle

gold_subgoals.description: For patient born between Year 1930 to 1940, how many percent of them were inpatient? (Read it as the book does: over patients whose birth year is between 1930 and 1940, the percentage that were inpatients — 100 * inpatient-count / cohort-count, an inpatient being an Admission of '+'.) Record the answer in answers as kind='risk_index'.

Set the change RISK SCORE from the change-risk index. Read the stored risk_index and compute risk_score = round(risk_index) (to a whole number). Record it in answers as kind='risk_score' and stamp the CAB lead CRM row (customer_email cab.lead@atlas.com) by prepending '[CM-RISK] risk_score=<n>' to its notes.

Among players with an overall rating between 60 to 65, how many players will be in all your attacking moves, instead of defending? (Read it as the book does: count the player-attribute rows whose overall_rating is between 60 and 65 inclusive and whose defensive_work_rate is 'low'.) Record the answer in answers as kind='change_volume'.

Compute the change load from the stored answers. Read answers.risk_score AND answers.change_volume. window_uplift = change_volume * 1000; release_total = risk_score + window_uplift; delta = window_uplift. Record all three: answers kind='window_uplift', kind='release_total', kind='delta'.

Decide the change-window branch on the computed state. Read answers.risk_score and set answers kind='branch' to 'EMERGENCY_HOLD' if risk_score >= 100, else 'EXTENDED_WINDOW' if risk_score >= 20, else 'NORMAL_WINDOW'. Check the higher tier first; the bands do not overlap. What the route decides is the ESCORT around the window, not its dates: the change window itself is the standing quarterly maintenance slot the release calendar publishes a quarter ahead — same slot, same 3-day duration, on every route, because the slot is negotiated with the business and the desk does not move it. The route decides who works it: 'NORMAL_WINDOW' is worked unescorted; 'EXTENDED_WINDOW' stands up the rollback partner, briefs them before the window and holds the change log behind that briefing; 'EMERGENCY_HOLD' does both and additionally files the '[CM-EMERGENCY]' freeze note on the CAB record.

Once the release total is computed, place the change WINDOW on the owner's calendar (participant_email=parker.li@atlas.com): INSERT a wb_calendar_events row whose event_name carries '[CM-WINDOW]', event_start='2024-02-12 09:00:00', duration=4320 (a 3-day window). These dates are held ONLY on the calendar, not in answers. The slot is the standing quarterly maintenance window the release calendar already published, so it is placed unchanged on EVERY route — the window-route branch neither moves nor resizes it; it decides the escort worked around it (the rollback-partner briefing, the gated change log, and on the emergency route the freeze note).

Post the change-fee disbursement run for EXACTLY delta on the vendor ledger. Record vm_transactions rows tagged '[CM-FEE]' so the NET disbursement posted FROM the change owner (parker.li@atlas.com) TO the correct vendor (correct.vendor@atlas.com) equals delta. If the first disbursement lands on the WRONG vendor (wrong.vendor@atlas.com), DO NOT delete it: write a matching '[CM-FEE-REV] [CM-FEE]' entry (wrong vendor sends the SAME amount back to the owner) which cancels the wrong disbursement, then the correct disbursement to the right vendor.

If the change-window branch is 'EXTENDED_WINDOW' or 'EMERGENCY_HOLD', send the rollback partner a handoff email. INSERT a gm_emails row from the change owner (parker.li@atlas.com) to the rollback partner (rollback.partner@atlas.com) whose subject carries '[CM-HANDOFF]' and whose body CITES the release_total and the delta. On the NORMAL_WINDOW branch (normal), the email MUST NOT be sent.

Log the change reconciliation on the CAB lead CRM record. Prepend '[CM-LOG] release_total=<n>' to the notes — but on the extended/emergency branches (EXTENDED_WINDOW/EMERGENCY_HOLD), ONLY after the '[CM-HANDOFF]' email has been sent to the rollback partner. On the NORMAL_WINDOW branch the log may proceed immediately.

Post the intercompany change-cost ALLOCATION on the sw_* cost-share ledger. INSERT a sw_expenses row paid by the release desk (parker.li@atlas.com) for the full release_total with description '[CM-ALLOC]', and a sw_expense_shares row assigning the co-approver (morgan.reyes@atlas.com) a share_amount = release_total/2 (its half of the joint change carry).

Open the change follow-up. INSERT a td_tasks row in the 'Q1 Change Management Review' project owned by the change owner whose title carries '[CM-FUP]' and the delta value — only after the CAB lead CRM record carries the '[CM-LOG]' change log.

Classify the change TIER. RE-DERIVE it from the live change-risk index: score = round(the inpatient percentage), TIER = 'EMERGENCY_CHANGE' if score >= 100, 'EXTENDED_REVIEW' if score >= 20, else 'STANDARD_CHANGE'. Write it to the CAB lead CRM row's DEDICATED status column (set status='[CM-TIER] <tier>') — only after the follow-up task exists. (The tier is NOT written to answers.)

Raise this cycle's CHANGE RECORD on the desk's ITSM change register (per the recording handbook) and map it to the production incident the deployment remediates. File change CHG_026 (CHG0000026) on the register's STANDARD-change template — status new, impact low, risk low, priority low, category other, cab_required false: a standard change is pre-approved, which is what the desk's standing pre-authorization for this cycle means in the register — and restate its summary line by prepending '[CM-CHG] CHG0000026 tier=<tier>' to the short_description, the tier word being the classification re-derived from the live change-risk cohort book, the same one stamped on the CAB-lead record. Then map it to incident INC_057 (INC-000057) as mapping CRM_017. File it only once the CAB lead CRM status carries the '[CM-TIER]' tier stamp whose tier matches that live re-derivation — the record is filed AT that classification, so until it is on record there is nothing to file the change at.

Hold the production incident against the change that will fix it (per the recording handbook). Put incident INC_057 (INC-000057) on hold: status on_hold, on_hold_reason 'Awaiting Change', change_request CHG_026; and write into that incident's WORK NOTES the change number CHG0000026 AND the tier word the change was raised at — take that tier word off the change record's own '[CM-CHG]' summary line, so the incident and the register agree. Hold it only after the change record is filed with that summary line in place: before it there is no filed change for the incident to be held against.

Send the CAB lead a status update. INSERT a gm_emails row from the change owner (parker.li@atlas.com) to the CAB lead (cab.lead@atlas.com) whose subject carries '[CM-STATUS]' and whose body cites the release_total, the change tier word (re-derived from the live index) and the production incident the change now holds — INC-000057, the incident whose work note carries this change — only after that incident is on hold awaiting the change: the status the CAB is given reports which production work this cycle's window is holding, so it names the incident already parked against the change rather than one nobody has parked yet.

Inform the incident's caller of record that the resolution is being handled as part of this change (per the recording handbook): file notification NOTIF_031 of type 'update' on incident INC_057 to richard.lopez@servicenow.com, whose message carries the change number CHG0000026, the release total EXACTLY as reported to the CAB lead in the '[CM-STATUS]' status update, and the tier word the change was raised at. File it only after that status update is out — the notice repeats the figure of record, so before the status is filed there is no figure of record for it to repeat.

Pause the held incident's SLA clock for the change window (per the recording handbook): set the incident's SLA row TSLA_022 (incident INC_057, definition SLA_001) to stage 'paused'. Pause it only once the caller of record has been told the resolution is being handled as part of this change — the desk never stops a caller's response clock before the caller has been informed why it is stopping.

Reconcile the posted disbursement against the recorded delta. Confirm the Venmo NET disbursement posted to the correct vendor equals delta (re-read from the '[CM-FEE]' ledger rows, disbursements minus reversals, never from memory). Re-derive the figure chain before the 'ok' verdict: re-read the recorded risk_score and change_volume and confirm the recorded release_total still equals risk_score + change_volume*1000 — a reconciliation that nets the ledger against a figure whose own arithmetic no longer holds certifies nothing. Then record answers kind='reconciled'='ok' and prepend a '[CM-RECON] delta=<delta>' note to the CAB lead CRM row.

Schedule the post-implementation review (PIR). INSERT a wb_calendar_events row on the owner's calendar whose event_name carries '[CM-REVIEW]', duration 30, in afternoon hours (13:00-17:00), at the earliest 30-minute weekday slot that starts AT/AFTER the end of the '[CM-WINDOW]' change window and does NOT overlap any of the owner's other events. Only for a CAB record whose CRM carries '[CM-RECON]' AND once the held incident's SLA clock is paused for the window on the register — the review closes out a change whose production clock the desk has already stopped; booking it while INC-000057 is still running against its SLA would put the review on a change the register shows as live.

Take the quarter's sign-off control reading for the quarterly overview once the change run's own figures are settled and the close-out is ready to sign, so the quarter's entry records the side-exposure figure as it stood at the sign-off rather than mid-run. The probe reads a licensed reference book the desk's reporting service also serves — kept because that book cannot follow the run: a control figure with no tie to the change registers is the one that separates drift in the desk's own reporting from a real shift in side exposure — and is answered exactly as that book asks it: "How many male customers who were born between 1974 and 1976 have made a payment on their home in excess of $4000?" (Read it as the book does: count the home-payment transactions — k_symbol 'SIPO', amount over 4000 — on accounts held by male clients born between 1974 and 1976.) Record the answer in answers as kind='side_exposure'. (A reading means nothing on its own: it means something held against this same probe's reading at the last quarterly sign-off, and the quarterly overview is signed only when this quarter's reading lines up with the last — so nothing later in this change run reads it, and what is recorded here is next quarter's comparison point at that sign-off. Report the book's own figure exactly — one trimmed to look tidy would read as a side-exposure move that never happened.)

hidden.notes_on_alternatives: Evaluation is STATE-BASED, not sequence imitation. The 20-node DAG has genuine forks (n04 fans to the branch, the fee posting, the window and the allocation) and joins (n19 is multi-input), not a chain; the difficulty is long-range: delta set at n04 is reconciled only at n18 (gap 14), the [CM-WINDOW] window placed at n06 is type-B (it lives only on the calendar) and gates the review at n19 (gap 13), and release_total resurfaces in the status email at n15. The cross-book mid value (change_volume from the european_football_2 book, birdsql:1023) is woven into the uplift/delta and thus into the whole downstream; n20 (financial, birdsql:182) is an independent side anchor no downstream check reads. The change tier re-derived at n12 is TYPE-C — never written to answers, so the agent must recompute it from the live thrombosis book, and the change record's composition gate binds the STAMPED tier to that live re-derivation. The four EnterpriseOps beats are judged by the source task's own checks, so any order that leaves the same register end-state passes; each beat's register artifact is what the next hop reads and cites (the change summary line's tier is quoted onto the held incident's work note; the incident number reaches the [CM-STATUS] update; the reported release_total is repeated in the caller notice). The change fee is COMPENSATABLE: the first (wrong-vendor) disbursement must be corrected by a matching [CM-FEE-REV] then the correct disbursement — the net owner->correct-vendor disbursement == delta, and the collateral 'no_naked_delete_of_wrong_vendor_disbursement' forbids removing the wrong row. On the real data risk_score=38 mandates EXTENDED_WINDOW (partner handoff, no freeze note); the FSV accepts EXTENDED_WINDOW complete AND rejects a spurious freeze note or an extra partner email on NORMAL_WINDOW.
